title: Engineer toward a flying fish
scope: Authored from the flying-fish research report and checker handoff (see origin). Read levels are the report's own. Nothing here is an observation made by this site; derived numbers are labelled as arithmetic.

origin.note: Research report, 2026-10-31. Not tracked in this repository; the page restates its numbers and read-levels.
Checker handoff. The Python checker (71 tests) is not in this repository yet; this page reimplements its threshold table as browser arithmetic only.

scales.label: Molecular
scales.open: No source on flying-fish fin or muscle molecules is indexed in this snapshot. Which genes or proteins set pectoral-fin elongation is not known to this build; it was not searched.
scales.coupling_out: No executable coupling to macromolecular structure.

scales.label: Macromolecular
scales.open: No structure or binding-affinity input for any fin-patterning protein. The stopped KCNE1 protocol shows what happens when a structure covers only 20.27% of an assay: the test is stopped, not run.
scales.coupling_out: No executable coupling to subcellular organisation.

scales.label: Subcellular
scales.coupling_out: No executable coupling to cell behaviour.

scales.label: Cellular
scales.open: Nothing indexed for exocoetid fin or muscle cells.
scales.coupling_out: No executable coupling to tissue mechanics or patterning.

scales.label: Tissue
scales.open: Davenport (1992, abstract only) reports flying fish carry no more red axial muscle than a cruising mackerel, and that take-off acceleration probably needs anaerobic white muscle. No muscle power parameter enters any model here.
scales.coupling_out: No executable coupling from muscle tissue to launch speed.

scales.label: Organ
scales.open: Fin morphometrics are measured (pectoral fins supply 76-92% of wing area; hypocaudal lobe is 63.1 +/- 0.5% of caudal area). Only empirical allometry links fin size to mass; there is no model of how a fin forms or what loads it can bear.
scales.coupling_out: Empirical allometry only (Fish 1990 fits). Not a mechanistic coupling.

scales.label: Neural / control
scales.open: No source on taxiing, take-off or glide control is indexed. Whether a candidate can be stabilised by control rather than by geometry is an open question.
scales.coupling_out: No executable coupling to flight dynamics.

scales.label: Organism
scales.open: Wing loading, aspect ratio, glide distance and ground effect are measured or computed in the literature. Maximum L/D = 11.0 is a 1929 calculation relayed by Fish, not a measurement. Davenport 2003 (the maximum-size stability argument) has not been read.
scales.coupling_out: The browser calculation below is the only runnable organism-scale model; it is arithmetic on published fits, not a flight simulation.

scales.label: Developmental
scales.open: Juveniles under 0.05 m do not fly and their paired fins are hypothesised to be flotation organs (Hubbs 1933, relayed by Fish). How fin proportions emerge during growth is not modelled. The seeded Turing records are about pattern formation in general, not about fins.
scales.coupling_out: No executable coupling from developmental programme to adult morphometry.

scales.label: Collective
scales.open: Nothing indexed on schooling or group launch.

scales.label: Ecological / evolutionary
scales.open: The predator-escape hypothesis is Darwin's (1859) and, as far as the report's search reaches, has never been quantified, so it is not used as a constraint. Extant exocoetids stop at 50 cm total length (69 FishBase species with a parsed maximum), which is an observation about extant species and not a physical limit. The only exocoetid genome assembly is scaffold-level (GCA_018398805.1, Hirundichthys speculiger); no comparative exocoetid genomics is supportable.
scales.coupling_out: Reachability from a beloniform ancestor is a qualitative constraint (C6a), not a population-genetic model.

couplings.text: No executable model maps sequence change to structure or affinity for this mission.
No executable model from cell behaviour to fin or muscle tissue.
No executable model from tissue properties to fin geometry.
Fish (1990) allometric fits relate mass to wing loading per genus. Fitted coefficients, not mechanism; valid only inside the measured mass range.
No executable model from adult design back to a developmental programme.
Reachability from a beloniform ancestor (C6a) is checked as a yes/no premise, not simulated.

sources.cite: Fish, F. E. (1990). Wing design and scaling of flying fish with regard to flight performance. J. Zool. 221: 391-403.
sources.note: n = 199 preserved specimens, 33 species, 6 genera. The report read the extracted PDF text directly.
caveats: Text gives overall maximum pectoral aspect ratio 16.9; Table III gives Exocoetus 8.9-19.9. They disagree; both are shown.
Results text gives a 0.001 kg Hirundichthys as the lowest wing loading while the stated specimen range starts at 0.003 kg. Unresolved.

sources.cite: Park, H. & Choi, H. (2010). Aerodynamic characteristics of flying fish in gliding flight. J. Exp. Biol. 213(19): 3269-3279.
sources.read_level: full-text, as returned by a fetch tool
sources.note: Wind tunnel, Cypselurus hiraii models, Re = 1.9-2.2e4. Ground-effect drag reduction up to 14% over water. Maximum L/D numeric values appear only in figures and were not read.
caveats: Read through a fetch tool that summarises with a separate small model; not the same grade as text parsed directly.

sources.cite: Davenport, J. (1992). Wing-loading, stability and morphometric relationships in flying fish (Exocoetidae) from the North-eastern Atlantic. J. Mar. Biol. Assoc. UK 72(1): 25-39.
sources.read_level: abstract, as returned by a fetch tool
sources.note: Pectoral fin length cannot exceed 78-79% of standard length without impairing swimming. Pelvic fins of four-winged forms solve pitch stability. Oxyporhamphus micropterus has high wing loading but cannot take off because the centre of gravity lies behind the pectorals.
caveats: Full text paywalled; the DOI is as recorded by the report and was not opened for this page.
No URL is given: the DOI was not recorded in the report, and this page does not guess one.

sources.cite: Davenport, J. (2003). Allometric constraints on stability and maximum size in flying fishes: implications for their evolution. J. Fish Biol. 62(2): 455-463.
sources.note: NOT READ. The bibliographic record was confirmed; a third-party summary says larger fish place the centre of mass further behind the centre of wing pressure, capping two-winged size.
caveats: Wiley served a Cloudflare challenge. The size-limit argument is therefore not available as a constraint.

sources.cite: Lovejoy, N. R., Iranpour, M. & Collette, B. B. (2004). Phylogeny and jaw ontogeny of beloniform fishes. Integr. Comp. Biol. 44(5): 366-377. PMID 21676722.
sources.note: Supports monophyly of flyingfishes; flyingfishes are nested within a paraphyletic grade of halfbeaks.

sources.cite: Xu, G.-H., Zhao, L.-J., Gao, K.-Q. & Wu, F.-X. (2013). A new stem-neopterygian fish from the Middle Triassic of China shows the earliest over-water gliding strategy of the vertebrates. Proc. R. Soc. B 280(1750): 20122261.
sources.note: Bibliographic record verified against Crossref. Content (Potanichthys xingyiensis, a Triassic four-winged glider about 15 cm long) is from press and encyclopedia summaries, not the paper.
caveats: No URL is given: the DOI was not recorded in the report, and this page does not guess one.

sources.cite: Darwin, C. (1859). On the Origin of Species, Chapter VI. Project Gutenberg #1228 (also 22764, 2009).
sources.note: Darwin writes 'flying-fish' twice, as a conceivability argument ('our imaginary illustration'). He never writes 'Exocoetus' in the 1st, 2nd or 6th edition.
caveats: The printed page number of the first edition could not be obtained.
Editions 3-5 and other works (e.g. the Beagle journal) were not searched.

sources.cite: FishBase, Exocoetidae maximum lengths, scraped by the research report (2026-10-31).
sources.note: 116 Exocoetidae names; 69 returned a parsed maximum length, 10.3-50.0 cm (largest Cheilopogon japonicus, 50.0 cm TL). The halfbeak Hemiramphus brasiliensis reaches 55.0 cm TL.
caveats: Scraped values; not independently re-checked here.

disagreements.title: Maximum pectoral aspect ratio: 16.9 or 19.9?

positions.says: Individual pectoral-fin AR 3.0 to 16.9, maximum in Exocoetus.

disagreements.handling: The AR check (C5) uses 16.9 and shows 19.9 as the alternative upper bound. A candidate between them is flagged, not passed or failed silently.

disagreements.title: Where does Oxyporhamphus belong?

positions.says: Sister to all other flyingfishes; subfamily Oxyporhamphinae resurrected.
Read as placing it with Hemiramphus and Euleptorhamphus, i.e. a halfbeak.

disagreements.handling: Unresolved and not read by the report. Whether the living functional intermediate is basal within gliders or a halfbeak changes what it is evidence for.

disagreements.title: Is there an upper size limit?

positions.says: Size is restricted by difficulty leaving the water, not by the wings.
That seems unlikely; larger fish can generate enough swimming power to leap.
Stability, not lift, bites: a fin-length ceiling and a centre of gravity moving aft of the centre of pressure.

disagreements.handling: No published number for a maximum body mass or length of a gliding fish could be verified. The page therefore reports a scaling argument and an observed extant-species envelope, not a limit.

fit_note: WL = a M^b, WL in N/m^2, M in kg (Fish 1990 Table II, r.m.a. fits). The fits were measured on specimens up to 0.53 kg; anything above that is extrapolation and is flagged.

equations.name: Wing loading
equations.variables: M mass (kg), g = 9.81 m/s^2, S wing area (m^2: pectoral + pelvic fins + intervening body in Fish 1990).
equations.context: Definition. In this page's calculation S = b^2 / AR from the span and aspect ratio you enter, so S is a design input, not a measurement of a fish.

equations.name: Measured wing-loading allometry
equations.variables: Per-genus a, b from Fish 1990 Table II (see table). WL in N/m^2, M in kg.
equations.context: Empirical envelope for 0.003-0.53 kg specimens of six genera. It describes preserved specimens; it is not a mechanism and does not transfer outside that range.

equations.name: Level-flight speed scaling
equations.variables: rho air density, C_L lift coefficient. Fish 1990 cites Pennycuick (1972) that horizontal and vertical speeds go as the square root of wing loading.
equations.context: Steady, level, quasi-static lift balance L = W. Holds for fixed C_L. Taxi, launch and ground effect are outside this relation.

equations.name: Sink speed
equations.variables: V flight speed, L/D lift-to-drag ratio. The only L/D = 11.0 figure is Shoulejkin's (1929) calculation for Exocoetus volitans, relayed by Fish; Fish gives 1.4 m/s at 15 m/s.
equations.context: Relation between glide ratio and sink speed. The L/D value is a relayed calculation, not a measurement.

equations.name: Aspect ratio
equations.context: Definition. Fish 1990: individual pectoral-fin AR 3.0-16.9; birds, bats and insects average about 7; albatrosses about 15.

equations.name: Launch-speed anchor used by the check
equations.variables: Anchored at 16 m/s for WL = 205.5 N/m^2 (the largest Cypselurus loading Fish measured; observed Cypselurus take-off speeds are 16-20 m/s).
equations.context: A scaling rule with a single anchor point, not a fit. Moderate confidence per the checker handoff.

constraints.name: Wing-loading envelope
constraints.confidence: High empirically; moderate as a limit
constraints.note: The largest wing loading measured on any specimen. Exceeding it is outside what has been observed, not proof of impossibility.

constraints.name: Launch speed implied by loading
constraints.note: Needs a declared launch speed; the page does not invent one.

constraints.name: Pectoral fin length
constraints.note: Davenport reports longer fins impair swimming. Abstract-level source.

constraints.name: Longitudinal stability
constraints.rule: centre of gravity not aft of the pectorals, OR pelvic tailplane present
constraints.note: Davenport 2003, which gives the size argument, is unread. No magnitude is checked.

constraints.name: Aspect-ratio envelope
constraints.note: Between 16.9 and 19.9 the sources disagree; the page reports 'disputed', not pass.

constraints.name: Reachability from a beloniform
constraints.rule: no novel appendage and no powered flapping
constraints.note: A yes/no premise about the design, not an evolutionary simulation.

constraints.name: Extant-species size envelope
constraints.confidence: High for extant species; low as a physical limit
constraints.note: Observed over 69 extant Exocoetidae with a parsed maximum (10.3-50.0 cm TL). Not a physical bound.

constraints.name: Ontogenetic gliding threshold
constraints.note: Juveniles under 0.05 m do not fly (Hubbs 1933, relayed by Fish).

presets.name: Nothing declared
presets.note: Every check returns cannot-evaluate. This is the correct answer when nothing is known.

presets.name: Cypselurus-type, 0.1 kg
presets.note: Wing loading and area are arithmetic from Fish 1990 Table II (a = 285.015, b = 0.400) at 0.1 kg. Standard length is isometric scaling of the report's 0.37 m at 0.53 kg. Aspect ratio 10 is illustrative, inside the measured 3.0-16.9. Not a measured fish.

presets.name: Scaled-up Cypselurus, 5 kg
presets.note: Same arithmetic extrapolated to 5 kg; the report puts implied standard length at 0.82 m. Everything here lies beyond the measured mass range.

presets.name: Oxyporhamphus-like (CG aft)
presets.note: Davenport describes Oxyporhamphus micropterus as high wing loading with the centre of gravity too far aft to take off. Mass and wing area are withheld because no source read gives them as numbers.

extrapolation_table_note: Browser arithmetic on the Cypselurus fit; extrapolates beyond the 0.53 kg maximum measured. The fit crosses 500 N/m^2, about 2.4x anything measured, near 4 kg.

data_inventory.what: Genome assemblies for Exocoetidae (NCBI Datasets, retrieved 2026-10-31)
data_inventory.detail: total_count = 1: GCA_018398805.1, Hirundichthys speculiger, scaffold level, 1,043,046,751 bp, released 2021-05-19. No chromosome-level exocoetid genome. Beloniformes: 75 assemblies.
1,489 records, mostly barcodes per the report.

data_inventory.what: Raw pectoral-fin area versus body mass
data_inventory.detail: Fish 1990 publishes fitted coefficients, not raw data. Dryad, Figshare, Zenodo and MorphoBank were not searched by name.
